facts.statement: For f(x)=x², the reduced nonzero-h quotient is 2a+h and f'(a)=2a for every real a.
f(x)=x has nonzero-h difference quotient ((x+h)-x)/h=1 and derivative 1 for every real x.
For h!=0, ((x+h)^3-x^3)/h = (3x²h+3xh²+h³)/h = 3x²+3xh+h² -> 3x² for every real x.
c'=0. Integer n>=1: (x^n)'=n*x^(n-1) for real x. n=0 means constant 1. Negative integers require x!=0. For real n the stated safe domain is x>0.
conditions: Do not infer endpoint derivatives from the safe-domain formula
The n=0 branch never evaluates 0*x^(-1) at zero

facts.statement: (1/x)'=-1/x² for x!=0; the two branches are not joined.
conditions: Original quotient also requires h!=0 and x+h!=0

facts.statement: sqrt x is defined for x>=0 and differentiable for x>0 with derivative 1/(2sqrt x). At zero its right difference quotient diverges to +infinity.
conditions: No ordinary finite derivative at zero

facts.statement: For a>0 and real x, (a^x)'=a^x ln a. a=1 is permitted and constant. e^x has derivative e^x.
conditions: The standard limit (a^h-1)/h -> ln a is invoked, not proved

facts.statement: For x>0, (ln x)'=1/x and (log_a x)'=1/(x ln a), where a>0 and a!=1.
conditions: The inverse local increment argument uses a nonzero exponential derivative
Constant multiple is explained locally and generalized in chapter 03

facts.statement: (sin x)'=cos x, (cos x)'=-sin x for all real x measured in radians.
conditions: Standard radian limits sin h/h->1 and (cos h-1)/h->0 are invoked
Geometric plots illustrate the formulas rather than proving those limits
